title: Short Course on Experimental Models of Human Cancer
text:
Cancer remains a largely incurable disease and the mouse remains a key model for human cancer. Thus, this
short course proposes to accelerate the understanding of the next generation of cancer investigators in cutting
edge modeling of human cancer including experimental cancer models, modern technology to assess
mechanisms and outcomes, testing of emerging cancer therapies, and the contributions of the tumor and host
genetics, as well as tumor microenvironment including its interplay with the immune system. The course will
promote networking and multi-disciplinary collaboration, and will inform and train junior investigators in state-of-
the-art approaches for conducting rigorous studies that utilize and leverage models of human cancer.

title: Ambystoma Genetic Stock Center
text: APPLIED RESEARCH COMPONENT - PROJECT SUMMARY This component addresses the significance and need to generate new assays and approaches for disease monitoring within the AGSC and beyond, and the need to generate and centralize information for diagnosing and treating axolotl diseases. Next generation 16S rRNA sequencing will be performed to increase breadth of pathogen monitoring and generate baseline microbial data in support of microbiome research, both of which will better ensure the health and reproducibility of AGSC axolotl lines. Additionally, an axolotl disease manual will be developed to provide a reference that axolotl labs can use to monitor pathogens and diagnose common axolotl diseases. The manual will include protocols, assays, and treatments curated from the literature and developed in house. Accomplishment of this sub aim will provide an essential resource for characterizing lesions in diseased and genetically modified axolotls that serve as models of human disease.

title: Molecular mechanisms of incubation of methamphetamine craving
text:
There are currently no FDA-approved therapeutics for psychostimulant use disorders, and our understanding
of the neurobiological changes underlying the intensification of methamphetamine craving over increasing
periods of abstinence is limited. The role of key projections from the nucleus accumbens in mediating the
incubation of methamphetamine craving will be delineated. This project will also use state of the art molecular
techniques to identify cell type-specific changes in gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the rat
nucleus accumbens associated with the incubation of methamphetamine craving.

title: Multi-Center Academic-Industrial Partnership for Personalized Al-Enabled High Count PET
text:
Through this multi-center AIP project, we will develop a robust deep learning-based software solution and
integrate into the clinical PACS system to convert any clinical PET image into a high-quality counterpart with
much lower image noise levels that can only be obtained with >90min long scan or extremely long field-of-view
scanners. The translation into PACS servers with “one-button” convenient workflow will lead to fast clinical
adoption and substantially benefit clinical practice to improve diagnostic accuracy and increase decision
confidence.

title: Learning Precision Medicine for Rare Diseases Empowered by Knowledge-driven Data Mining
text:
Recent advances in precision medicine have accelerated research in rare diseases and overwhelmed
clinicians’ capacities to manage and leverage the latest knowledge efficiently in clinical practice. This project
will build a novel informatics framework that leverages semantic knowledge discovery and data mining
techniques to assist rare disease differential diagnoses with the goal of shortening the diagnostic odyssey
associated with rare diseases.

title: Identifying and disabling new pathways for macromolecular recycling in pancreatic cancer
text:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal cancer that thrives in a nutrientdeprived, oxygen-
poor environment. We identified two critical lysosomal hydrolases, PLBD1 and LGMN, which are essential for
PDAC growth and metastasis, with PLBD1 disrupting lysosomal function when ablated and LGMN being crucial
for liver colonization. This proposal will explore how the degradative functions of these hydrolases promote
PDAC survival, growth and metabolism, and will develop targeted inhibitors, potentially pointing to new
therapeutic strategies.

title: Microbiota, Probiotic and Dietary Metabolite Control of Enteric Pathogen Virulence
text:
Metabolites from the microbiota, probiotics and diet can inhibit the virulence of bacterial pathogens, but their
mechanisms of actions have been not fully elucidated. Using innovative chemical biology, proteomic and gene
editing methods, we will determine the protein targets of prominent bacterial and dietary metabolites and
evaluate how they attenuate the virulence mechanisms of bacterial pathogens. Understanding how key
metabolites affects bacterial pathogenesis may afford new therapeutic targets and anti-infective agents.

title: Simultaneous PET/phMR studies on interplay of mGlu/dopamine receptors in PD-like neurodegeneration
text:
Research of the brain receptor functions holds a promise for better diagnostic tools and drugs
that could be tailored to the individual needs, thereby eliminating or reducing side effects and
even providing a way for prevention of disease. Real time imaging of receptor modulation using
simultaneous phMRI and PET will challenge the present theories of signaling and synaptic
plasticity during degenerative processes. The results of receptor modulation can be readily
utilized in the drug development for dopamine-glutamate regulation related disorder, like
Parkinson’s disease, schizophrenia or drug abuse.

title: Genetic determinants of AAV liver transduction and toxicity
text:
Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector-mediated gene delivery has been successfully used in patients with liver
targeting, however, liver toxicity with decreased transgene expression was observed in some patients after
AAV systemic administration. In this application we will study the role of genetic background in AAV liver
hepatotoxicity using collaborative cross mice in a hope of developing more effective and safer AAV vectors for
future clinical applications with AAV liver targeted gene delivery.

title: Threading the needle: Development of Novel MR Methods for Effective Control of an Emerging Lipophilic Tumor Therapy
text:
Public Health Relevance/ Project Narrative
 Resistant cancers such as glioblastoma and pancreatic cancer remain incurable despite major advances in
genetics and immunotherapies. Our group has been studying cancer using a model in which cancer is
approached as an aberrant form of wounding and posits that unless healing is actively induced that eradication
will remain an insufficient strategy. This proposal is based on the observation that a lipid drug emulsion of
oxidized CoQ10 (BPM31510) possesses features that suggest it can eradicate in vivo glioblastomas if
administered at the precise dosage and this proposal seeks to develop imaging strategies that will focus on
identifying metabolic and redox signatures associated with response and failure of this strategy.

title: Developing a novel adenine base editor tool for in vivo alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency gene correction.
text:
Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a genetic disorder that can cause lung emphysema and liver fibrosis in
patients. This proposal seeks to evaluate the safety of a gene editing approach to correct the most common
genetic cause of AATD and determine its potential to reduce liver and lung disease burden in a mouse model of
AATD. This work will facilitate the clinical development of gene editing strategies to treat AATD.

title: Control of insulin secretion by Rho-kinase
text:
The malfunction of pancreatic β-cells is a significant risk factor for type 2 diabetes, and its cause remains
unclear. Our research indicates that inhibiting Rho-kinase in pancreatic β-cells significantly blocks insulin
secretion and glucose tolerance. The Kim and Kulkarni teams will collaborate to explore Rho-kinase's
novel role in pancreatic β-cell metabolism, and the findings of this study could lead to the discovery of a
potential target for new treatments of diabetes and its related metabolic disorders.

title: Stem Cell and Transplantation Biology
text: Our goal is to assist investigators, especially trainees and junior faculty from across the US, in their studies of hematopoiesis and biology of non-malignant disorders so that their work may lead to better understanding of these disorders. To achieve this goal, we need to build a strong work force of emerging and experienced investigators to fuel synergistic collaborations that advance our understanding of hematopoiesis and stem cell biology. The tools needed to advance this science may be out of reach for many young and even some more experienced investigators, so we aim to provide access to resources at reduced rates, funds for pilot studies, and a virtual community of supportive colleagues.

title: Biomarker Reference Laboratory (BRL)
text: Project Summary/Abstract – Biomarker Reference Laboratory The proposed BCC will develop sensitive genomic and proteomic tests for the early detection of ovarian cancer in uterine lavage samples. The genomic component will assess genome-wide methylation, and the proteomic component will assay proteins using the proximity extension assays (PEAs) which provide relative quantitation between samples. The test will be optimized on samples from a training cohort. The methylation signal will be aggregated and optimized across the genome using machine learning approaches by the biomarker developmental lab (BDL). Optimization of the proteomic component will identify a custom panel of up to 21 proteins for absolute quantitation. The Biomarker Reference Laboratory (BRL) will work with Fulgent Genetics to ensure that optimized methylation signal and the custom panel of protein assays comply with CLIA/CAP standards and achieve analytical performance metrics specified by the BRL. The PI of BRL has extensive experience in ensuring assays in her clinical biochemistry lab serving the University Health Network, the largest in Canada, achieve clinical grade before analysis of patient samples are implemented in the lab’s workstream. The BRL will apply similar standards, agreed upon by all investigators in the BCC, to the methylation aggregated signal, the custom panel, and the classifier formed by combining the methylation signal with the protein abundances in the custom panel. This test using the classifier combining the genomic and proteomic signals, qualified with these standards, will give the highest probability of success for a test for the early detection of ovarian cancer when applied to uterine lavage samples from an independent validation cohort, and to cervical swabs as a readily accessible biospecimen with high patient acceptability.

title: Determinants of reservoir contraction and expansion in vivo, ex vivo, and in vitro
text:
RELEVANCE (See instructions):
Our proposal studies why HIV reservoirs decay at different rates in various cohorts of HIV-infected 
individuals on antiviral therapy. We hypothesize that reservoir contraction and expansion occur 
simultaneously in all HIV-infected individuals making the reservoir appear stable. We propose to perturb 
these forces and use a machine learning analysis to identify the drivers behind them and to ultimately 
reduce the size of the HIV reservoir.

title: Genomic Characterization and Clinical Outcomes of Cancers in WTC-Exposed Survivors & Responders
text:
The September 11, 2001 World Trade Center disaster exposed approximately 400,000 rescue workers, recovery
workers, and lower Manhattan residents to a complex mixture of cancer-causing substances, and these
individuals continue to develop cancer at rates above the general population more than two decades later. This
study will use advanced tumor sequencing to determine how this toxic exposure shaped the cancers that
developed in affected individuals, and whether it affects how those cancers respond to treatment. Findings will
enable doctors to better identify which WTC-exposed cancer patients are at highest risk and to tailor their care
accordingly.

title: Multifunctional Imaging of the Optic Nerve Head in Glaucoma
text:
Current imaging strategies cannot identify the spatial correlations between early-stage structural remodeling and
vascular changes in the optic nerve head, hindering our understanding of glaucoma mechanisms and limiting
diagnostic and treatment improvements. This gap motivates the development of multifunctional optical
coherence tomography, which enables simultaneous, high-resolution visualization of microstructural and
vascular architecture in the eye. This proposed project combines baseline data collection using a translational
imaging technique with mechanistic investigation of glaucoma progression using a custom-built high-end imaging
system, aiming to advance the understanding of glaucoma pathophysiology while improving early detection and
monitoring of disease progression.

title: RNA folding and catalysis at the interface of biophysics and genomics
text:
This MIRA project will help predict RNA folding in vivo and provide insight into the dynamics of RNA
folding under in vivo-like conditions and in the cell. It will also help discover and elucidate novel functions
for RNA enzymes and RNA motifs with rare charged and tautomeric bases. This work helps understand
RNA gene regulation and identifies RNA targets for therapeutic tools.

title: Nonviral Delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 into Hepatocytes Combined with APAP Selection for Treatment of Familial Hypercholesterolemia
text:
Liver transplantation is the only definitive therapy available for treatment of inherited metabolic diseases affecting
the liver, but it has severe drawbacks. We aim to directly compare different delivery approaches for introducing
gene editing reagents into hepatocytes combined with a novel approach for selecting edited hepatocytes in the
liver using transient administration of acetaminophen as a novel treatment for familial hypercholesterolemia. We
will study the repopulation potential, capacity of edited hepatocytes to overcome immunity to gene editing
reagents in the liver, and extent that our approach reverses the disease in a mouse model.

title: Novel regulation of vascular dementia
text:
Cardiovascular disease and dementia are major health problems, particularly in the elderly population. Vascular
pathologies across all vasculature are linked to dementia of all causes, particularly the two major subtypes,
Alzheimer’s dementia (AD) and vascular dementia (VaD). The current application seeks to fill the scientific gaps
by uncovering a novel function of smooth muscle cell (SMC)-expressed Runx2 in regulating
cardio/cerebrovascular pathologies and VaD, and developing a novel paradigm underlying the Runx2-dependent
signaling network in regulating SMC phenotypic switch. Results from these studies should also have important
clinical implications in developing potential strategies for maintaining vascular integrity and improving cognitive
function and quality of life.
